ex: The director makes a short cameo in his own movie.
Did you see the singer's cameo in that film?
Fans loved the surprise cameo at the end of the show.
She has a small cameo in the last episode.

magnum.note: Most often in "magnum opus": the best work of an artist or writer.

render.note: Most often a verb meaning "make" or "give": "The rain rendered the road unsafe."

ex: She has an opal ring from her grandmother.
The opal shines with many different colors in the light.
Is this a real opal or just colored glass?
Her necklace has a large blue opal in the middle.
Anthrax is a dangerous disease of animals and people.
Farmers vaccinate their cattle against anthrax every year.
People can catch anthrax from sick sheep or cows.
The doctor tested the farmer for anthrax.

RPG.note: Stands for "role-playing game"; can also mean a rocket launcher.

peri.note: A rare word from Persian stories. Most often seen in "peri-peri", a hot chili sauce.

anemia.note: Uncountable: "She has anemia" (not "an anemia"). British spelling: "anaemia".
ex: Her tiredness was caused by anemia.
Eating more iron can help prevent anemia.
The doctor tested him for anemia last week.
Anemia is common in women during pregnancy.

indie.note: Most often used before a noun: "an indie band", "indie games".
ex: She mostly listens to indie and some old rock.
This summer festival is great for fans of indie.
Is this song indie or pop?
There is a lot of good indie on this radio station.
"Eureka! I finally found my car keys!" she shouted.
He jumped up and shouted, "Eureka! The code works!"
I had a eureka moment while I was in the shower.
"Eureka!" said Anna when she solved the last puzzle.

slash.note: Most often a verb: to cut with a long, fast move, or to cut a lot: "They slashed prices."

ex: The cafe is full of hipsters with laptops.
He looks like a hipster with that beard and hat.
Hipsters love vintage clothes and old vinyl records.
This part of town is popular with young hipsters.

jacuzzi.note: In the US, often called a "hot tub".

touchscreen.note: Also written as two words: "touch screen".

standby.note: Most often "on standby": ready to act if needed: "Doctors are on standby."
ex: Press this button to put the TV on standby.
The printer goes into standby after ten minutes.
Does the computer use much power on standby?
Turn the TV off completely, not just to standby.

Sanskrit.note: Always with a capital letter, no article: "She is learning Sanskrit."

madonna.note: Most often a name. As a word: a picture or statue of Mary; usually "the Madonna".

oval.note: Most often an adjective: "an oval table", "an oval face".

tender.note: Most often an adjective: soft or gentle: "tender meat". In the US, "bid" is more common for this.
ex: The city announced a tender for the new bridge.
Our company won the tender for the school building.
Five firms took part in the tender this year.
When does the tender for the road repairs close?

dashboard.note: Also the panel in front of the driver in a car.

dunk.note: Also a verb: to put food into a drink: "dunk a cookie in milk".

armageddon.note: Often written with a capital letter: "Armageddon".

flannel.note: Uncountable as cloth: "made of flannel". In British English, a flannel is also a washcloth.
ex: He wore a warm flannel shirt in the cold.
Flannel sheets are cozy in the winter.
This shirt is made of soft, thick flannel.
Do you have any pajamas made of flannel?

emoji.note: Plural is "emoji" or "emojis"; both are used.

rally.note: Most often a big public meeting or protest: "a peace rally in the square."

liner.note: Often "ocean liner". It can also mean a thin layer inside something: "a trash can liner".

edict.note: Formal word; "order" or "decree" is more common.

ex: The fans were in euphoria after the big win.
A feeling of euphoria came over her at the finish line.
The euphoria after the concert did not last long.
Some runners feel euphoria after a long run.
Let's play frisbee in the park after lunch.
Our dog can catch a frisbee in the air.
I threw the frisbee too high, and it hit a tree.
Can you bring the frisbee to the beach tomorrow?

carousel.note: At airports, a carousel is the moving belt where you get your bags.
ex: The kids rode the carousel at the fair.
Can we go on the carousel one more time?
The carousel plays old music while it turns.
She sat on a white horse on the carousel.
